title: Refit a wardrobe rail between a closed and an open end support
instruction: Fit the wardrobe rail into its two end supports.
context: Wardrobe rails sit between a closed end support on one side panel and an open U support on the other. The rail is cut a few millimetres short of the gap, but it is still too long to go in level: the end must be fed into the closed support with the rail tilted, then the rail is swung down into the U. People do this whenever a rail is taken out to clear a wardrobe or has been knocked out of its supports.
setup: Positions in cm from the arm-base line (x forward) and the midline (y left), one fixed layout matching the screenshot. Wardrobe section, fixed to the table: white melamine particleboard, base board 20 x 63.6 x 1.8 cm and two side panels 20 cm deep, 1.8 cm thick, 16 cm tall, inner faces 60.0 cm apart, both from x 22 to 42, centred on the midline. Left panel (y +30): a closed chrome end support, an oval cup modelled as a 2.1 x 3.8 cm bore 1.0 cm deep, axis 8.0 cm above the table at x 32. Right panel (y -30): an open chrome U support at the same axis, 2.1 cm wide inside, 1.5 cm deep from the panel, floor 6.5 cm above the table, cheeks 3 cm tall, open on top. Rail: an oval steel wardrobe tube 3.0 cm tall x 1.5 cm wide, 59.2 cm long, 0.35 kg, chrome, lying left-right with its tall side vertical on two blue foam blocks (6 x 6 x 5 cm), the blocks centred at x 16, y +10 and y -10, the rail centred on the midline at x 16.
scoring: Final state only, with both grippers open and at least 3 cm from the rail and the rail still (moving under 1 mm) for the last 1 s; otherwise 0. 0.4 if the left end is at least 0.8 cm into the closed support's bore. 0.4 if the right end rests on the U support's floor (end centre within 0.3 cm of the support axis height, at least 0.5 cm over the floor). 0.2 more if both ends are in and the rail is level within 1 degree. Full score 1.0.
reset_notes: Lift the rail's right end out of the U, slide the left end out of the closed support, and lay the rail back on the foam blocks.
fidelity: Rigid bodies built from boxes. The oval tube is a 3.0 x 1.5 cm rectangular bar and the supports are rectangular bores, with 0.3 cm clearance each side and 0.4 cm top and bottom. The wardrobe section is one fixed 25 kg part. Friction 1.2 everywhere. No screws or fixings are modelled.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (the rail stays on the foam blocks; the run stopped at about 2,000 steps when the Dream-1 session expired); demo: 1.0
